<strong><h4>Overview </h4></strong>
<br>
  •	<strong> Source of these data </strong>
<br>
This is a view into the information provided in
the research article
  <a href=https://annalsofglobalhealth.org/articles/10.5334/aogh.5145 target=_blank>
  <br>
  Particulate Air Pollution, Disease, and Death in the Cities and Towns of Southwestern Pennsylvania,
  <br>
  <strong>
E. M. Whitman,
L. Bryan,
S. Sehdev,
P. J. Landrigan
</strong></a>

<hr>
  •	<strong>Areas Shown: </strong>The areas shown in the map on the left are census tracts
<br>for the Pittsburgh  Metropolitan Statistical Area (8 counties, 739 tracts).
<br> The numbers presented on the histogram to the right
<br> are estimates obtained from models based on the year 2016,
<br>the most recent year for which this fine-grained data was available.
<hr>
  •	<strong>Health Harms </strong> The health harms reported in this study are attributable to PM 2.5 exposure.
<br>
  Much of this harm occurs even when PM 2.5 exposure levels are below the current federal standard of 9.0 µg/m³.
<br> For more information about these measures of harm, click on the information buttons along the left edge of the right panel.
<br>
  This indicates that the federal standard needs to be reduced to protect the health of vulnerable populations,
<br>
  especially those near steel mills and coke ovens like Clairton and Braddock.
